history.text: Verne Gagne beat Édouard Carpentier in Omaha; Nebraska affiliates recognized it, creating a disputed version.
related: Omaha version of the World Heavyweight Championship

history.text: Los Angeles-based NAWA recognized Carpentier as NWA champion while gradually splitting from the NWA.
Freddie Blassie beat Carpentier, creating the basis for the Los Angeles WWA title.
related: WWA World Heavyweight Championship (Los Angeles version)

history.text: The Omaha version was unified with the AWA World Heavyweight Championship.
The Los Angeles title ceased to exist when the WWA returned to the NWA.
related: WWA World Heavyweight Championship (Los Angeles version)

history.text: JCP controlled many NWA territories and limited title matches to its contracted wrestlers, making the title effectively exclusive.
Turner completed its purchase of JCP and began converting it into WCW, which stayed in the NWA.
On television, the NWA World Heavyweight Championship was portrayed as the WCW World Heavyweight Championship.
Ric Flair was fired from WCW while still recognized as NWA champion and kept the NWA belt.
The NWA board stripped Flair of the NWA title shortly after he signed with the WWF.
The NWA board authorized a tournament using the Big Gold Belt, won by Masahiro Chono.
WCW recognized the unauthorized Flair–Tatsumi Fujinami title change from March 21, 1991.
WCW withdrew from the NWA, kept the belt, and lost the right to use the NWA name.
The WCW International World Heavyweight Championship was unified with the main WCW title.
The NWA revived the Ten Pounds of Gold belt to represent a new champion after losing WCW.
Shane Douglas won the NWA tournament, then ECW withdrew from the NWA and Douglas was stripped of the title.
Chris Candido won a second NWA tournament, and the title was recognized in SMW and USWA.
The NWA made a deal to appear on WWF television; WWF ended it in less than a year.
Jeff and Jerry Jarrett licensed the NWA World Heavyweight title for NWA-TNA; Dan Severn was stripped.
TNA withdrew from the NWA but kept rights to the title until its agreement ended on May 13, 2007.
Adam Pearce won the vacant title in a tournament held to fill the gap left by the TNA split.
NWA rights transferred to International Wrestling Corp, which moved the NWA to a licensing model.
Colt Cabana beat Adam Pearce in Melbourne after the NWA refused to sanction the match.
Corgan's ownership of the NWA took effect, and the title was renamed the NWA World's Heavyweight Championship.
The NWA began transitioning into a standalone promotion with a weekly series, later named NWA Powerrr.
